blocks.text: Ties a rope to a spar in seconds, and starts or finishes nearly every lashing. Learn it first.

blocks.heading: How to tie it
items: Take the end round the spar.
Cross it over the standing part and take it round the spar again, beside the first turn.
Tuck the end under the turn you have just made, so it comes out between the two turns, beside the standing part.
Pull both ends tight and push the turns snug against each other.

blocks.heading: It's right when
items: Both ends come out from under the same crossing turn.
The ends point in opposite directions.
The back shows two neat turns side by side.

blocks.text: A clove hitch can slip or roll when the spar turns or the pull comes from the side. For anything that takes weight, add a half hitch round the standing part.

title: Round turn and two half hitches
cast: For guy lines, and tying to a post or a ring

blocks.text: Ties a rope to a pole, a peg or a ring so it holds under a steady pull, and it can be tied or untied while the rope is still taking the strain.

blocks.heading: How to tie it
items: Take the end round the pole twice. These two turns are the round turn, and they take the strain.
Bring the end over the standing part, round it and back through, to make a half hitch.
Make a second half hitch the same way, just below the first, going round in the same direction.
Slide both half hitches up to the round turn and pull tight.

blocks.heading: It's right when
items: The two half hitches look like a clove hitch round the standing part.
There is a full round turn against the pole, not just one turn.

title: Timber hitch
cast: For dragging a log, and for starting a diagonal lashing

blocks.text: Grips a spar or a log when pulled, and falls apart easily when the pull stops. It starts the diagonal lashing.

blocks.heading: How to tie it
items: Take the end round the spar.
Pass it round the standing part.
Twist the end back round its own part at least three times, so the twists lie along the spar.
Pull on the standing part until the loop grips the spar.

blocks.text: It only holds while it is under strain. That is what makes it quick to undo afterwards.
Ties the two ends of one rope round something, like a bundle or a bandage. It lies flat and unties easily.

blocks.heading: How to tie it
items: Right end over left end, and under.
Left end over right end, and under.
Pull both ends to tighten.

blocks.heading: It's right when
items: Each end comes out beside its own standing part.
It lies flat, like two interlocking loops.

blocks.text: Never use a reef knot to join two ropes that will take weight: it can shake loose. Use a sheet bend.

title: Sheet bend
cast: Joins two ropes, even of different thickness

blocks.text: Joins two ropes together, and still holds when one is much thicker than the other.

blocks.heading: How to tie it
items: Make a bend (a U shape) in the end of the thicker rope.
Bring the end of the thinner rope up through the bend from underneath.
Take it round behind both sides of the bend.
Tuck it under itself, but not back through the bend.
Hold the bend and pull the thinner rope tight.

blocks.heading: It's right when
items: Both short ends finish on the same side of the knot.

title: Bowline
cast: A loop that will not slip

blocks.text: Makes a fixed loop in the end of a rope that will not tighten or slip, and still unties after taking a load.

blocks.heading: How to tie it
items: Make a small loop in the standing part, with the part nearest the end lying on top. This is the rabbit's hole.
Bring the end up through the small loop from underneath: the rabbit comes out of the hole.
Take the end round behind the standing part: round the tree.
Bring it back down through the small loop: back down the hole.
Hold the end against the side of the big loop, and pull the standing part to tighten.

blocks.text: Leave a good length of tail, and check it before anyone relies on it.

title: Square lashing
cast: Two spars crossing at right angles

blocks.text: Holds two spars that cross at right angles, like a ledger across the legs of a frame. The lashing most builds use.

blocks.heading: How to lash it
items: Tie a clove hitch on the upright, just below where the crosspiece will sit. Twist the short end round the rope so it is out of the way.
Take the rope up over the crosspiece, behind the upright, down in front of the crosspiece and behind the upright again. That is one wrap.
Make three or four wraps, pulling each one tight. On the crosspiece each wrap goes outside the last; on the upright, inside.
Make two or three frapping turns: wind the rope between the two spars, round the wraps, and pull hard. This is what tightens the lashing.
Finish with a clove hitch on the crosspiece.

blocks.heading: It's right when
items: The wraps lie flat and side by side, not crossing each other.
The frapping turns pull the wraps in tight between the spars.
The spars do not twist when you push them.

title: Diagonal lashing
cast: Two spars that cross but do not touch, or want to spring apart

blocks.text: Pulls together two spars that cross but are not touching, such as the braces on a trestle. It starts with a timber hitch that draws them together.

blocks.heading: How to lash it
items: Tie a timber hitch round both spars, diagonally across the crossing, and pull it tight to draw the spars together.
Make three or four wraps along the same diagonal as the timber hitch.
Make three or four wraps across the other diagonal.
Make two frapping turns between the spars, round the wraps, and pull hard.
Finish with a clove hitch on one spar.

title: Shear lashing
category: Side by side · Scouts and up
cast: Two spars side by side, opened into an A

blocks.text: Joins two spars side by side so they can be opened out, like the top of an A-frame or a pair of sheer legs.

blocks.heading: How to lash it
items: Lay the two spars side by side. Tie a clove hitch round one of them.
Make eight to ten wraps round both spars. Keep them fairly loose, or the spars will not open.
Make two frapping turns between the spars, round the wraps.
Finish with a clove hitch on the other spar.
Open the spars out. The lashing tightens as they open.

title: Round lashing
category: Side by side · Scouts and up
cast: Joins two spars to make a longer one

blocks.text: Joins two overlapping spars into one longer one, for a flagpole or a long handrail. Always use two, well apart.

blocks.heading: How to lash it
items: Overlap the two spars by at least a metre. Tie a clove hitch round both of them.
Make eight to ten tight wraps round both spars.
Finish with a clove hitch round both spars. There is no gap between the spars for frapping turns.
Tie a second round lashing near the other end of the overlap.

blocks.text: Binds three spars together so they open into a tripod: the start of a wash stand, a cooking crane or a flagpole base.

blocks.heading: How to lash it
items: Lay three spars side by side, with the middle one pointing the other way.
Tie a clove hitch round one of the outside spars.
Weave the rope over and under the spars in a figure of eight, six to eight times. Keep it loose.
Make two frapping turns in each gap between the spars.
Finish with a clove hitch on the other outside spar.
Cross the outside legs over the middle one and stand the tripod up.

blocks.text: The frame behind most bigger builds. Bridges, chariots and gateways are mostly A-frames joined together, so teach this one first.

blocks.heading: Safety check
items: Check every spar for cracks, splits and soft or rotten wood. Put bad ones aside.
Do not use rope that is frayed, soft or mouldy.
Nobody climbs on, sits on or swings from the frame until a leader has checked every lashing.
Carry spars low in camp, and call out before you swing one round.

blocks.heading: How to build it
items: Lay the two legs side by side on the ground, tips level.
About 30 cm down from the tips, tie a **shear lashing** round both legs. Keep the turns fairly loose.
Open the legs into an A until the bottoms are about 1.5 m apart.
Lay the ledger across both legs, 30 cm up from the bottom, and **square-lash** it to each leg.
Stand it up and push the top gently. Tighten any lashing that slips, then have a leader check it.

blocks.text: Two A-frames and a walkway make a bridge.
Keeps the wash bowl off the ground and at a height where nobody has to crouch. A good first build for a patrol.

blocks.heading: Safety check
items: Check the staves for cracks before you start.
Stand it on level ground, and try it with an empty bowl before filling it.

blocks.heading: How to make it
items: Tie a **tripod lashing** round the three long staves, about 30 cm from their tops, and stand them up as a tripod.
Square-lash the three short staves across the legs, at the height the bowl should sit, to make a triangle.
Rest the bowl in the triangle. If it is loose, move the short staves up the legs until it sits snugly.
